title: Why airport runways are so long

items.ask: How long is an airport runway?

items.label: Big airport runway
items.ask: Why do runways need to be so long?

explain.say: An airliner has to reach roughly 250 to 330 kilometres per hour before its wings make enough lift to take off. Speeding up that much takes a long run, far longer than a football pitch.

items.label: Big airport runway
items.ask: Why do runways need to be so long?

explain.say: Small propeller planes can use an airstrip under a kilometre long. Big jets need far more, and the runway must also leave room to stop safely if a take-off is abandoned at high speed.

items.label: Big airport runway
items.ask: Why do runways need to be so long?

explain.say: Main runways at big airports are often three to four kilometres long. Heavy, fully fuelled jets on hot days need the most, because hot, thin air gives the wings and engines less to work with.

faq.q: Why do runways need to be so long?
faq.a: A jet must speed up to well over 250 kilometres per hour before it can lift off, and the runway must also leave enough length to stop if the take-off is abandoned at high speed.

faq.q: How long is an airport runway?
faq.a: Small airstrips can be under a kilometre long, while main runways at large international airports are usually about 3 to 4 kilometres long and 45 to 60 metres wide.

faq.q: Why do planes need more runway on hot days?
faq.a: Hot air is thinner, so the wings make less lift and the engines less thrust at a given speed. The plane must go faster over the ground and needs a longer run.
asks: Why do hot or high airports have long runways?

faq.a: Qamdo Bangda Airport in Tibet, more than 4,300 metres above sea level, has one of the longest public paved runways, about 5,500 metres, because the thin air there makes take-offs much longer.
asks: Which airport has the longest runway?

faq.a: A heavy airliner puts enormous loads through its wheels, so runways are built from thick layers of concrete or asphalt over strong crushed-rock bases, much deeper than an ordinary road.

facts: Qamdo Bangda Airport in Tibet, about 4,334 metres above sea level, has a paved runway about 5,500 metres long.
Runway numbers come from their compass direction: runway 09 points roughly east, at 90 degrees, and its other end is runway 27.

quiz.say: Why might the same plane need a longer runway on a hot afternoon than on a cold morning?
quiz.show: More runway on a hot day because…

options.show: Hot air is thinner, giving less lift
options.say: Hot air is thinner, giving less lift

options.show: Pilots are tired in the afternoon
options.say: Pilots are tired in the afternoon

quiz.why: Thinner air means the plane must reach a higher ground speed to get enough lift, so it needs a longer take-off run.

wrong.1: Runways barely change length with temperature, and heat would make them slightly longer, not shorter.
wrong.2: Take-off distance depends on physics, not tiredness.
